text:
customer_jane: Hey @support -- since yesterday's rollout our production traffic started returning inconsistent answers for the same user session. Same prompt, same session_id, multiple different outputs across consecutive requests. Very visible for our FAQ chatbot. We're seeing hallucinations that weren't there before.

support_alex: Sorry about that, Jane. Can you paste one reproducible request (curl) + the exact responses you saw? Also include session_id, request_id if available. We'll escalate. :eyes:

customer_jane: Here's minimal repro (redacted keys):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-prod-v2","input":"What is the refund policy for late returns?","session_id":"sess-9a7f3","max_tokens":120}'
```
Responses from three back-to-back requests (copied verbatim):
1) "Our refund policy: no refunds after 24 hours..."
2) "We don't offer refunds for digital goods, please contact support."
3) "Refunds are processed within 5-7 business days. See policy: https://..."
All from the same process, within ~8 seconds. Request IDs from response headers: r-84f1, r-84f2, r-84f3.

support_alex: Thanks. Can you confirm whether you recently enabled 'variant_fallback' or changed routing rules? Any canary/rollout flags on your account?

customer_jane: We didn't change anything client-side. We did notice a Redwood Console spike yesterday when you rolled v2 as default, but nothing toggled on our end.

support_alex: Copying eng-runtime and eng-ml. @eng_cheng @eng_mike please triage routing/fallback. Sounds like per-request routing is sending different model variants within the same session.

eng_cheng: Looking. Can you share the full response headers (we need x-route-variant, x-model, x-request-id) and any proxy logs? Also which region (us-west-2?).

customer_jane: Region us-west-2. Full headers for r-84f2: 
```
x-request-id: r-84f2
x-model: open-prod-v2-qa-2026-03
x-route-variant: fallback-quant
content-type: application/json
```
For r-84f3:
```
x-request-id: r-84f3
x-model: open-prod-v2
x-route-variant: primary
```

support-bot: NOTE: recent control-plane change at 2026-03-16T22:00Z enabled gradual rollout policy 'v2-default-swap' with variant_fallback=true for 10% of traffic during warmup.

eng_mike: That control-plane note matches. Variant_fallback=true explains different x-route-variant values. But shouldn't a session stay pinned to a variant? We have session affinity keys based on session_id, but affinity TTL is 15s by default. If customer is issuing rapid back-to-back requests, and affinity ping was missed, we might re-evaluate routing and pick fallback.

eng_cheng: Reproducing locally with session_id sess-9a7f3 and our routing simulator: if affinity TTL expires between requests, policy can select fallback variant (quantized model) to reduce cost. The quantized fallback has slightly different decoding behavior leading to the hallucination delta.

support_alex: To be clear: customer sees mixed outputs because some requests hit primary, some hit fallback quantized variant. That matches the sample.

customer_jane: This is bad for our UX. Can you (1) pin our sessions to the primary model while this rollout stabilizes, or (2) disable variant_fallback for our tenant? We need deterministic behavior.

eng_mike: We can temporarily disable fallback for the tenant. Requesting SRE to apply rule to override 'variant_fallback' for tenant t-corp-jane. @sre_anil can you apply?

sre_anil: I can do that. Will add tenant override: variant_fallback=false for t-corp-jane in routing config and push. ETA ~7 minutes. Will also check if affinity pings are being lost due to intermittent timeouts.

eng_cheng: Also opening a follow-up: we should increase affinity TTL for session-based APIs to 60s for customers using session_id, or at least surface the TTL in the Console and SDK. Filing issue INF-3421.

support_alex: For the immediate customer: SRE please confirm once override is live and we will ask Jane to repro. Also include a log search for the three request IDs so we can confirm variants pre/post-change.

sre_anil: Override deployed to routing layer for t-corp-jane. I see logs: r-84f1 -> route=quantized-fallback at 22:14:05, r-84f2 -> route=quantized-fallback at 22:14:13, r-84f3 -> route=primary at 22:14:19. After override, new requests should always map to primary.

customer_jane: Trying again now... (re-sent same curl 3x)
customer_jane: All three responses now match and look correct. Thank you.

support_alex: Glad that helped. We'll keep this override until rollout completes and we'll follow up with the product/console team to add clearer controls and sessions TTL.

eng_mike: Action items: (1) INF-3421 change affinity TTL and expose in SDK/Console, (2) add a tenant-level toggle in Console for 'allow_variant_fallback' (security/ops), (3) add a regression test that compares primary vs quantized variant outputs on our eval prompts to detect semantic drift.

customer_jane: Appreciate the quick response. Please keep me posted on permanent fix timeline.

support_alex: Will follow up in this thread once INF-3421 and the tenant toggle are scheduled. For now leaving override until rollout completes. :white_check_mark:
